 Judgment

The petitioners in O.P.(M.V.) No.969/2010 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pala,
are the appellants herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).

They are the wife and minor daughter of the deceased Thomas,
who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 03.08.2010.The above O.P
was filed under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act.

2. According to the petitioners, 03.08.2010, while the deceased was travelling in a scooter through Ponkunnam - Kottayam public road, a police van bearing Registration No.KL-01/X-9998 driven by the 1 st respondent, in a rash and negligent manner hit against the scooter.
As a result of which, he sustained fatal injuries and he succumbed to the injuries on the same day.
3. The 2nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the police jeep.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A8 and X1.
No evidence was adduced MACA NO. 704 OF 2014 2025:KER:10851 by the respondents.
6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.3,93,500/-.

7. Heard Sri.Abraham Mathew, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners/appellants and Smt.S.L.Sylaja, the learned Government Pleader appearing for the State.
8.
In the claim petition, the monthly income of the deceased was claimed as Rs.3,330/- per month.
However, the Tribunal assessed his monthly income at Rs.3,000/-, without assigning any valid reasons.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie during the year 2010 will come to Rs.7,500/-.

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the Tribunal was not justified in fixing the notional income of the deceased at Rs.3,000/-.
Therefore, his notional annual income, for the purpose of assessing the compensation is fixed at Rs.40,000/-.
11. As per the IInd scheduled to the Motor Vehicles Act, the compensation payable to the legal representatives of the deceased within the age group 30 to 35 is Rs.6,40,000/-.
Out of which, 1/3rd is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.

After deducting 1/3 rd the balance amount Sosamma @ Molly vs Hassan.T.S on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90231825/
2 will come to Rs.4,26,666/-.
The Tribunal has awarded only Rs.3,84,000/- towards loss of dependency instead of 4,26,666/-.
Therefore, the MACA NO. 704 OF 2014 2025:KER:10851 loss of dependency is revised to Rs.4,26,666/-.
The compensation awarded on the other heads are as per the schedule and there is no challenge on the same.

12. Therefore, the petitioners/ appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.4,36,166/-,
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.

 1 Funeral expenses 2000 2000  2 Loss of dependency 3,84,000 4,26,666  3 Loss of estate 2500 2500  4 Loss of consortium to the 5000 5000  first petitioner  Total 3,93,500 4,36,166  Amount enhanced 42,666  13.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 3rd respondent is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.4,36,166/- (Rupees Four Lakh Thirty Six Thousand One Hundred and Sixty Six Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 9% per annum, from the date of the petition till realisation/deposit, with proportionate costs,
within a period of two months from today

. 
MACA NO. 704 OF 2014 2025:KER:10851 14. On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioners, in the ratio fixed by the Tribunal, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
